title: Data sheet - CCS5, SCS5 & TSC
short_title: Terma CCS5, SCS5 & TSC data sheet
status_notes: Commercial product data sheet; no issue or date printed. The PDF metadata gives a creation date of 18 May 2018, which is not printed on the sheet.
summary:
A two-page commercial data sheet from Terma for three related spacecraft control and checkout products: SCS5 (multi-user operations version, used for all mission phases from operations preparation and launch to routine operations), CCS5 (multi-user checkout version, used within an EGSE for spacecraft assembly, integration and test) and TSC (a lightweight single-user version, for example for instrument or payload testing).

The sheet lists the functional scope: telemetry reception and frame processing (virtual channel filtering, gap detection, authentication, decryption), parameter monitoring and alphanumeric, graphic and synoptic displays, commanding with a manual stack, CLTU generation and COP-1 flow control, command verification history, archiving and retrieval, session management, reporting and hot redundancy. Automation uses the TOPE procedure language, which includes Tcl/Tk 8.6.

Of direct interest to MIB readers, the TM/TC database is described as the SCOS-2000 MIB ICD 6.9 'extended' (for example unlimited field lengths, multiple databases, deduced parameters in TM and TC, big- and little-endian parameters, VPD_CHOICE and dynamic housekeeping definitions); the command sequence tables are not supported. The archive is an open format of raw binary segmented files indexed in MySQL or PostgreSQL. Supported standards include ECSS-E-ST-50-01C/03C/04C, ESA PSS-04-106/107/151, several CCSDS Blue Books and PUS ECSS-E-70-41A; protocol drivers cover EDEN, C&C, ZDS Cortex, ESA NIS and SLE RAF and F-CLTU. It also describes a Qt-based user interface, an SVF mode, TM simulation and TC modelling, and the Windows and Linux platforms.

It is useful as evidence of how commercial EGSE products reuse the SCOS-2000 MIB as their database format.

key_points.text: SCS5 and CCS5 are multi-user products and TSC is the much lighter single-user version; CCS5 is used in EGSE for spacecraft assembly and integration testing, SCS5 for all phases of spacecraft operations.

Commanding features include a manual stack, CLTU generation, COP-1 handling and flow control, and command verification history; TM processing includes VC filtering, gap detection, authentication and decryption.

The TM/TC database is the SCOS2000 MIB ICD 6.9 'extended', for example with unlimited field lengths, deduced parameters in TM and TC, big- and little-endian parameters, VPD_CHOICE and dynamic HK definition.
TC sequence tables of the MIB are not supported; TOPE or command stack files are to be used instead. An online MIB table browser exists and all tables are accessible from TOPE.
Automation uses the TOPE language, which includes Tcl/Tk 8.6 and extension packages such as [incr Tcl].
Archive format: raw binary segmented files with header and content, with an index stored in an RDBMS (MySQL or PostgreSQL).
Listed PUS support is ECSS-E-70-41A; frame/packet coding standards listed are ECSS-E-ST-50-01C, 03C, 04C, ESA PSS-04-106, 107, 151 and CCSDS 102.0-B-5, 201.0-B-3, 202.0-B-3, 202.1-B-2 and 301.0-B-3.
Main protocols: EDEN and C&C for checkout/EGSE, ZDS Cortex and ESA NIS for ground stations, and SLE (RAF and F-CLTU) with the uNIS option.
Software platform is C++ on Qt 5.7 (commercial); runs on Windows (tested on Windows 7) and Linux (tested on RHEL7, installed as RPM).

notes: Two-column marketing data sheet; the text layer interleaves the two columns, so headings and lists appear mixed in the extracted text. The extracted text has a third, empty page after a trailing form feed; the PDF has 2 pages. No author is printed (the PDF metadata names a Terma author, not recorded here). Companion to the Terma presentation terma-ccs5-tsc-presentation. CCSDS standard titles are not printed, only their numbers.
